newsitem.title: CHILE: Two members of German enclave in Chile arrested.
newsitem.headline: Two members of German enclave in Chile arrested.

text.p: Police late on Monday arrested two members of a secretive German colony in southern Chile that has faced a series of charges of child abuse and kidnapping.

German citizens Hartmuth Hopp and Gerhard Zevalt were arrested at the settlement, Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony), tucked in the Andean foothills, on the orders of investigating judge Hernan Gonzalez, said police in the town of Parral.
The exact charges against the two men were not released.
But police said the arrests formed part of a general government investigation into allegations of sexual abuse of children in the colony.
The German-speaking enclave's founder and leader Paul Schaefer, the subject of an international arrest warrant, is believed to be holed up inside the heavily guarded community, police said.

Schaefer, who has not been seen in public in recent years, faces charges of sexually molesting at least five Chilean boys who attended a boarding school at Colonia Dignidad. He and other leaders of the colony, founded by Schaefer in 1961, face various other charges including illegal detention of children and obstruction of justice.
